items.title: Alvin Tedjo sworn in as Mississauga's new mayor
items.summary: It's the dawn of a new era of politics in one of Ontario's largest cities. Mississauga's city council was sworn in on Monday night, and new mayor Alvin Tedjo is promising to bring a hopeful vision for change to reality. CBC Peel reporter Dana Roberts has the story.

items.title: Mayor Tedjo doubles down on 2-year property tax freeze at new Mississauga council's inaugural meeting
items.summary: Alvin Tedjo toppled two political veterans in a hard-fought Mississauga mayoral election, and one of the key promises that helped propel him to victory was a two-year property tax freeze for all residents. At Mississauga’s inaugural council meeting on Monday night, Tedjo made it clear that he intends to keep that promise. “In my first act as Mayor, I am issuing a Mayoral Directive to city staff to officially begin the work to achieve a 0 per cent tax increase in the forthcoming 2027 budget, and the 2028 budget,” Tedjo said in his first address to council after swearing-in ceremonies concluded. ” Despite early polls showing a tight race leading up to election, Tedjo handily beat out former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish to take over the city’s top job. He had previously served as Ward 2 councillor and finished second in the 2024 mayoral byelection. Throughout the campaign, he argued that his two main rivals both made life more expensive for residents during their respective tenures. “The 2027 budget will be tabled in February, and will outline a fiscally responsible plan that will ease the burden on our residents and stabilize the household budgets of every family in Mississauga,” he said on Monday.

items.title: Officer worried about ‘ambush’ during fatal shooting on Mississauga man, inquest hears
items.summary: A police constable told a coroner’s inquest Monday he was concerned about the risk of an ambush as he approached a car that had crashed into a pillar after it was hit by police gunfire during a botched arrest in Mississauga nearly seven years ago. It was dark at the time and the car’s windows were heavily tinted, making it difficult to see inside, Peel regional police Const. Marc Charlebois, then a member of the force’s tactical unit, told the inquest into the death of Jamal Francique. m. on Jan. 7, 2020, and arrived at the townhouse complex about 20 minutes later, he said. As he came up toward the back of the car, carrying a ballistic shield more than a metre long and a metal bar designed for breaking or prying into windows, the officer said he and a colleague called out some commands, but there was no answer. Charlebois, who is the first witness in the inquest, said he managed to see the lone person in the car after breaking the rear passenger window. “I can just see the back of his right side, the right side of his head. … I can hear the male struggling for breath,” he said. Charlebois saw blood, he said, but didn’t yet realize Francique had a gunshot wound. There was no sign of movement, he said. ” inquest counsel Roger Shallow asked the constable.

items.title: OPP Says Driver Ramped Onto Tow Truck Deck Before Rollover Crash Near Mississauga's Dixie Road
items.summary: According to the OPP Highway Safety Division, a tow truck operator was struck and seriously injured on Highway 401 near Dixie Road on Sunday while assisting a disabled driver. Police say a third vehicle struck the tilt and lift tow truck, ramped onto its deck, hit the vehicle being loaded, and then rolled over. The tow truck operator was also struck and was rushed to hospital with serious, non-life-threatening injuries, police said. The OPP noted that starting Jan. 1, Ontario's move over rules will expand to cover certain stopped work vehicles with flashing amber lights, including Ministry of Transportation vehicles. Police said failing to slow down, move over or let an emergency vehicle pass can bring fines of 400 to 2,000 dollars, three demerit points and a licence suspension of up to two years.

items.title: Peel Public Health to Screen 27,500 Students' Vaccine Records Ahead of Spring 2027 Suspensions
items.summary: According to Peel Public Health, officials will review the vaccination records of roughly 27,500 students across the region's four school boards during the 2026-27 school year. The agency says the screening targets students from senior kindergarten through Grade 3 and in Grades 11 and 12, following an earlier round that suspended nearly 9,000 students for incomplete records. Families will get two notification letters over several months giving them a chance to catch up on missing shots before suspension orders are issued, Peel Public Health said. Suspensions tied to this round are scheduled to begin in spring 2027 for students who miss their deadlines, according to the agency. The enforcement falls under Ontario's Immunization of School Pupils Act, which requires vaccination against nine diseases, including measles, mumps and polio, unless a valid exemption is on file, the agency said.

items.title: Mayor Tedjo Directs Staff to Pursue Zero Percent Tax Hikes in 2027 and 2028 Budgets
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the newly elected Council was sworn in at an inaugural meeting at the Living Arts Centre, marking the start of the 2026-2030 term. The city says Mayor Alvin Tedjo and all members of Council made their declarations of office, administered by City Clerk Diana Rusnov. In his inaugural address, Tedjo announced his first Mayoral Directive, instructing city staff to work toward a zero per cent tax increase in both the 2027 and 2028 budgets, the city said. The mayor cited the rising cost of living, housing challenges and economic uncertainty facing residents and businesses, and said the city needs to find efficiencies and deliver value for taxpayers, according to the city. The city says the new council includes nine returning councillors and two newly elected councillors representing Wards 2 and 7, with members serving through November 14, 2030.

items.title: Peel District School Board's CEO to Retire Amid Ongoing Provincial Oversight of 145,000-Student System
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel District School Board Director of Education and CEO Rashmi Swarup is set to retire at the end of November, having announced the move on June 2. The outlet reports the board serves roughly 145,000 students across more than 260 schools in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, one of Ontario's largest systems. Swarup was appointed in 2021 during the board's first stretch under provincial supervision, which followed findings of systemic anti-Black racism and governance failures, insauga.com said. Her mandate included carrying out 27 binding provincial directives before that supervision ended in 2023, according to the outlet. The board has since been placed under provincial supervision a second time, and insauga.com reports her departure raises questions about who will run daily operations while the province remains in control.

items.title: 17-Year-Old Sought in Mississauga Man's Killing Also Wanted for Separate Barrie Murder
items.summary: According to Toronto Police, a 17 year old Toronto male already sought on a second degree murder charge in the Nov. 7 shooting death of Malik Abass, 18, of Mississauga, is now also wanted for first degree murder in the Nov. 10 killing of Brandon Blake, 18, of Barrie. Police said officers responding to a call early Nov. 7 found Abass suffering gunshot wounds and performed life saving measures before paramedics took him to hospital, where he died a short time later. The suspects fled the scene before police arrived, according to police. Toronto Police said Abass was the city's 33rd homicide victim of 2026. Police identified two suspects in Abass's death this past weekend and say the Canada wide warrants remain active, according to the force.
